messages:
mira: Heads up: our JS SDK Edge sample is tripping on two things in a pnpm monorepo: missing export at build time (esbuild) and TypeScript not finding types for the runtime subpath. Node runtime is fine.

jess: ugh. Is this the subpath export like '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge'?

mira: yup. Build error in Vercel: \"Package '@redwood/sdk' has no export named './runtime/edge'\". At the same time, TS in consumer app shows \"Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge'\".

nikhil: two separate but related issues: 1) pnpm isolated linker symlinks package into .pnpm/... which can confuse esbuild's export resolution; 2) TS needs a .d.ts exposed at that subpath or typesVersions/exports mapping.

laura: can you paste the SDK package.json exports+types bits?

mira: here's the minimal snippet:

```json
"main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "dist/esm/index.js",
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./runtime/edge": { "import": "./dist/esm/runtime/edge.js" }
}
```

mira: notice there's no types entry for ./runtime/edge so TS falls back and complains.

jess: yep. For TS you need to either: a) add a matching export for types (e.g., "./runtime/edge": { "types": "./dist/types/runtime/edge.d.ts", "import": ... }), or b) add a top-level ambient d.ts that declares module '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge'.

nikhil: and bundlers: when SDK is a symlink, esbuild sometimes resolves the file path under the symlink target and never consults the package.json exports. We reproduced with pnpm isolated. Switching to node-linker=hoisted fixed it for us.

laura: workarounds that don't force users to change linker: 1) add a root-level proxy file like runtime-edge.js that re-exports from dist and declare runtime-edge.d.ts that references the types; 2) add explicit exports entries for both the JS and types subpath; 3) add a small README note for pnpm users.

mira: I tried option 2 first and added this to package.json:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" },
  "./runtime/edge": { "import": "./dist/esm/runtime/edge.js", "types": "./dist/types/runtime/edge.d.ts" },
  "./runtime-edge": "./runtime-edge.js"
}
```

mira: then I added runtime-edge.js at package root with a tiny re-export and runtime-edge.d.ts that re-exports types. That fixed both esbuild (when imported as '@redwood/sdk/runtime-edge') and TS errors.

jess: for the example app we should switch to the runtime-edge proxy import to be robust. Also add types mapping so TS consumers who still use the subpath get d.ts resolution.

nikhil: repro steps I used locally attached here:

```bash
# fresh workspace
pnpm i
cd apps/next-edge-sample
pnpm run build # fails with esbuild export error when sdk is a symlink
# TS error snippet
pnpm dlx ts-node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.js'))"
# test hoisted mode
echo 'node-linker=hoisted' > .npmrc
pnpm install --force
pnpm --filter apps/next-edge-sample run build # succeeds
```

laura: CI suggestion: add matrix step that builds examples with both pnpm node-linker modes and runs tsserver checks. Catch regressions fast.

mira: opened PR on examples switching import and added quick note in README, plus a small sdk package patch that adds the types export for runtime subpath. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/95 (WIP).

ci-bot: Ran preview: built example in default (isolated) and hoisted modes; proxy import build passed in both. Typecheck job passed. :white_check_mark:

jess: long-term we should consider publishing a tiny compatibility doc that explains exports/types interplay for ESM/CJS dual packages in workspaces (pnpm/yarn/turbo). People hit this frequently.

nikhil: agreed. Also add a small unit test in SDK repo that validates package.json exports are visible when package is installed as a workspace (simulate symlink). We can run that in CI for fast feedback.

mira: filing follow-ups: 1) add CI matrix; 2) add SDK test for workspace exports visibility; 3) docs page. Linking this thread from the PR. Thanks all :raised_hands:
